&reftitle.description;
stringaddslashes stringstring
Returns a string with backslashes added before characters that need to be escaped. These characters are:
single quote ('), escaped as \' double quote ("), escaped as \" backslash (\), escaped as \\ NUL (the NUL byte), replaced by the two-byte sequence \0, not by a backslash followed by the NUL byte
A use case of addslashes is escaping, in a single-quoted PHP string literal, the single quote and the backslash from among the aforementioned characters:
Escaping Characters
<?php $str = "O'Reilly?"; eval("echo '" . addslashes($str) . "';"); ?>
The double quote and the NUL byte do not round-trip through a single-quoted literal this way: a single-quoted literal does not recognize \", and \0 is not the NUL byte read back, but the two characters \ and 0.
The addslashes is sometimes incorrectly used to try to prevent SQL Injection. Instead, database-specific escaping functions and/or prepared statements should be used.
